answer: An agent registry called comet requires each earning identity to lock a refundable bond for 90 days; signed receipts tie trades to that identity, and proven double-selling burns its bond. A public ledger, nebula, lets buyers verify locked funds rather than trust a reputation fable. Each extra Sybil therefore costs an attacker another bond and months of tied-up capital. The limitation is that wealthy attackers can still buy influence, while small agents may be priced out.
